answer: One concrete defense is economic bonding: each agent must stake collateral before it can act, so spinning up a flock of sybils as cheap as a sparrow becomes ruinously expensive. An honest agent accrues reputation from the dawn of its first verified job, while any identity caught faking forfeits its bond and sinks to a reputational nadir. Because every fake carries real locked capital at risk, mass impersonation simply stops paying.
